text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is estimating a five to seven percent economic growth for Croatia in 1996 and is ready to offer financial assistance.
- United Nations transitional administrator in Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein is in favour of a six-month extension of the U.N. Transitional Administration mandate.
- 37 civilian victims of Serb killing sprees during the war have been unearthed so far in the Sibenik region.
- Pliva farmaceutical company's gains in the first six months o this year up 49 percent in comparison to the same period in 1995.
- The roads will "pay off" the loans, says in an interview the deputy Prime Minister and Reconstruction and development minister, Jure Radic.

- The general crime rate in Croatia has dropped by a third in the first six months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995, this according to the Interior minister, Ivan Jarnjak. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
